deep.reconstruction:
PART 1 (Non-Archimedean systems have no cuts; fully legible, not crossed out). Claim: in a non-Archimedean ordered number system one may not assume that every (Dedekind) cut has a cut number. Setting: an ordered additive system with an element t>0 such that t, 2t, 3t, ... are all < some T (T is infinitely large relative to t). Suppose the cut defined below had a cut number, written ∞t. Lower class L = {x : x < nt for some suitable positive integer n} ('g.v.p. n', presumably 'ganze positive Zahl'). Upper class U = all other numbers. L is nonempty (it contains t), U is nonempty (it contains T), and every element of L is below every element of U, so this is a cut. ∞t is to separate the classes. (i) ∞t is not in L: if ∞t < nt, then (n+1)t is in L and exceeds ∞t, which is impossible (my step). So ∞t is the least element of U. (ii) ∞t − t < ∞t, so ∞t − t is in L. Hence there is an n with ∞t − t < nt. Hilbert writes '< n', a slip for nt. (iii) Then ∞t < (n+1)t, and (n+1)t is in L, contradicting (i). Conclusion: completeness (existence of cut numbers) forces the Archimedean property, so a non-Archimedean system cannot be Dedekind-complete.

PART 2 (remark). 'All my geometries and the results following from them come down to non-Archimedean groups.' This is a programmatic comment linking his independence models (non-Archimedean, non-Pascalian, non-Desarguesian, non-Legendrian geometries) to ordered non-Archimedean number systems or groups.

PART 3 (crossed out with an X). Problem: in Bolyai–Lobachevsky geometry, construct the line parallel to two given lines, i.e. the line joining their ends.
- The two given lines emanate from O and have ends α and β.
- Mark E on Oα and F on Oβ with OE = OF.
- Draw from E the parallel to OF (the ray Eβ) and from F the parallel to OE (the ray Fα).
- Bisect the angle at E between Eα and Eβ, giving line h; bisect the angle at F between Fβ and Fα, giving line k.
- Claim: the common perpendicular of h and k is the sought line αβ.
Justification (mine, modern): reflection in the bisector h of the doubly asymptotic triangle Eαβ swaps the rays Eα and Eβ, hence swaps the ends α and β. It therefore maps line αβ to itself with reversed orientation, so h ⊥ αβ; likewise k ⊥ αβ. Hence αβ is a common perpendicular of h and k, and is the unique one because h and k are ultraparallel.
Hilbert's own proof is by contradiction ('nimm das Gegentheil an'). In the figure the feet of the common perpendicular are A (on h) and C (labelled like 'G'), with B on the perpendicular. From A and C one draws parallels to OE; the resulting angles α and γ would be equal. He argues this is impossible, since otherwise AB ⊥ CB; the angle sum of triangle ABC is < 2 right angles, so ... The argument continues on the next page ('∠BAR > 1 Rechte ... the two lines from A and C would then not be parallel'), and that is also struck out. The next page then turns to constructing the common perpendicular of two ultraparallel lines by equal angles and segments.
errors: Slip: '∞t − t < n' should read '∞t − t < nt'. The conclusion '∞t < (n+1)t' shows nt was meant.
Implicit but harmless step: one must note that ∞t is not itself in the lower class (the lower class has no maximum), so ∞t is the least upper element and (n+1)t ≤ ∞t gives the contradiction.

The proof in the crossed-out part is incomplete and apparently abandoned; Hilbert struck it out. The construction itself is correct (bisectors of the angles at E and F are perpendicular to line αβ), so the X likely reflects dissatisfaction with the proof. A further gap: within his axiomatics the existence of a common perpendicular to h and k needs separate proof, which he begins addressing on the next page.

results.what: Dedekind completeness implies the Archimedean property; equivalently, in a non-Archimedean ordered system the cut {x : x < nt for some n} has no cut number.
results.modern_name: Complete ordered groups/fields are Archimedean (the set {nt} has no supremum)
results.usually_credited_to: Folklore going back to Dedekind (1872) and Stolz/Hölder; used by Hilbert in the Vollständigkeitsaxiom discussion (Grundlagen 1899/1900, 'Über den Zahlbegriff' 1900)

results.what: Remark that all his geometries (independence models) reduce to non-Archimedean groups or number systems.
results.modern_name: Coordinatization of non-Archimedean geometries by ordered non-Archimedean fields/groups
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (Grundlagen der Geometrie, 1899); Veronese for non-Archimedean geometry

results.what: Construction in hyperbolic geometry of the line joining the ends of two intersecting lines, via OE = OF, cross-parallels, angle bisectors h and k, and the common perpendicular of h and k.
results.modern_name: Existence/construction of the line joining two ends (line parallel to both sides of an angle)
results.usually_credited_to: Bolyai (Appendix, 1832) for the problem; this bisector construction appears in Hilbert, 'Neue Begründung der Bolyai-Lobatschefskyschen Geometrie', Math. Ann. 57 (1903) (Grundlagen, Anhang III)

deep.surprise_reason: A draft of material Hilbert published (completeness vs. Archimedes; the end-joining construction of his 1903 hyperbolic-geometry paper). It is of interest only as a working note showing an abandoned first proof.

checkable.asserts: In the upper half-plane with ends 0 and ∞ (line αβ = imaginary axis), at E=x+iy the circle |z|=|E| makes equal angles with the vertical ray to ∞ and the geodesic arc to 0. So the bisector at E is the geodesic orthogonal to αβ; expected result 0.

transcription_corrections: 'man[?] 2 Punkte E, F auf ihnen an' is more likely 'nimm 2 Punkte E, F auf ihnen an'.
'g.v.p. n' is an abbreviation, probably 'ganze positive Zahl n' (possibly 'ganze von Null verschiedene positive').
The image indeed reads '∞t − t < n'; this is an author's slip for 'nt', not a transcription error.
The point at the bottom right of the figure, read as 'G', is C (it is referred to as C in the proof).
'die aus[?] denselben folgenden Resultate' is plausibly correct ('aus denselben folgenden').
